symptom: PC in VLAN 10 cannot communicate with another PC in VLAN 10
topology_note: Two PCs connected to SW1 access ports Fa0/1 and Fa0/2; both should belong to VLAN 10
show_outputs: show vlan brief: VLAN 10 missing
expected_fault: VLAN 10 is not created on the switch

symptom: PC receives an IP but cannot reach devices in its VLAN
topology_note: PC connected to SW1 Fa0/5; port should be assigned to VLAN 20
show_outputs: show vlan brief: Fa0/5 appears in VLAN 1
expected_fault: Access port is assigned to the wrong VLAN

symptom: Users on one switch cannot reach users on another switch in the same VLAN
topology_note: SW1 and SW2 connected using Gi0/1 trunk link; VLAN 30 required across both switches
show_outputs: show interfaces trunk: VLAN 30 not allowed
expected_fault: VLAN 30 is missing from the trunk allowed list

symptom: Inter-VLAN communication fails for VLAN 40 users
topology_note: Router-on-a-stick connects R1 to SW1
show_outputs: show interfaces trunk: switch uplink operating as access port
expected_fault: Switch-router link is not configured as a trunk

symptom: PC can communicate locally but cannot reach remote networks
topology_note: PC in VLAN 10 uses R1 as default gateway
show_outputs: ipconfig: default gateway 192.168.20.1; VLAN 10 gateway is 192.168.10.1
expected_fault: PC has an incorrect default gateway

symptom: PC has valid IP but cannot ping its router gateway
topology_note: PC connected to SW1 access port in VLAN 20
show_outputs: ipconfig: 192.168.20.25/24; gateway 192.168.20.1; show ip interface brief: G0/0 192.168.30.1
expected_fault: Gateway address does not match the local subnet

symptom: Multiple PCs in the same subnet cannot reach the gateway
show_outputs: show ip interface brief: router interface G0/0 is administratively down
expected_fault: Router gateway interface is shut down

symptom: PC automatically receives an APIPA address
topology_note: DHCP server is located on another subnet behind R1
show_outputs: ipconfig: 169.254.10.22; show ip dhcp pool: available addresses remain
expected_fault: DHCP requests are not reaching the remote DHCP server

symptom: PC receives an address from the wrong subnet
topology_note: DHCP server has pools for VLAN 10 and VLAN 20
show_outputs: show ip dhcp binding: client receives 192.168.10.x while connected to VLAN 20
expected_fault: DHCP pool/network configuration is incorrect

symptom: Some clients receive addresses while others fail
topology_note: Large number of PCs share the same DHCP pool
show_outputs: show ip dhcp pool: maximum addresses exhausted
expected_fault: DHCP address pool has no available leases

symptom: PC has IP address but DNS server information is missing
topology_note: Clients obtain addresses from router DHCP
show_outputs: ipconfig /all: DNS Servers field is empty
expected_fault: DHCP pool does not provide a DNS server option

symptom: PC can ping a web server by IP but not by hostname
topology_note: DNS server is located at 192.168.50.10
show_outputs: nslookup: DNS request timed out
expected_fault: DNS server is unreachable or unavailable

symptom: Only one hostname fails while other domains resolve
topology_note: Client uses DNS server 192.168.50.10
show_outputs: nslookup internal.example.com: NXDOMAIN
expected_fault: DNS record for the requested hostname is missing

symptom: Clients cannot resolve any hostnames after DNS server change
topology_note: Network recently migrated to a new DNS server
show_outputs: ipconfig /all: DNS Server 192.168.60.10; ping 192.168.60.10 fails
expected_fault: Client cannot reach the configured DNS server

symptom: PC can reach its gateway but not a remote LAN
show_outputs: show ip route: no route to 192.168.20.0/24
expected_fault: R1 is missing a route to the remote network

symptom: Remote network is reachable from one router but not from another
topology_note: R1 and R2 connected through serial link
show_outputs: show ip route: route exists on R1 but missing on R2
expected_fault: Return route is missing on R2

symptom: OSPF neighbors are not forming
topology_note: R1 and R2 share network 10.0.0.0/30
show_outputs: show ip ospf neighbor: no neighbors
expected_fault: OSPF configuration does not include the connecting network

symptom: Traffic follows an unexpected path
topology_note: Three routers use OSPF
show_outputs: show ip route: unexpected next hop selected
expected_fault: Routing metric or route preference causes a different path

symptom: Default route is configured but internet network remains unreachable
topology_note: R1 connects internal LAN to ISP router
show_outputs: show ip route: no 0.0.0.0/0 entry
expected_fault: Default route is missing

symptom: PC can ping gateway but cannot access application server
topology_note: ACL applied inbound on router interface
show_outputs: show access-lists: deny tcp any host 192.168.40.10 eq 443
expected_fault: ACL explicitly blocks HTTPS traffic

symptom: Guest users can access internal server
topology_note: Guest VLAN should only access the internet
show_outputs: show access-lists: no deny statement for internal subnet
expected_fault: Guest isolation ACL rule is missing

symptom: SSH access to router is blocked for administrators
topology_note: Management subnet is 192.168.99.0/24
show_outputs: show access-lists: deny ip 192.168.99.0 0.0.0.255 any
expected_fault: ACL blocks the management subnet

symptom: Web application works but ping fails
topology_note: ACL is applied between client and server
show_outputs: show access-lists: deny icmp any any
expected_fault: ICMP is blocked by ACL while TCP traffic remains allowed

symptom: Internal PC can reach gateway but cannot reach internet
topology_note: Inside LAN uses private 192.168.10.0/24 addresses
show_outputs: show ip nat translations: empty; show ip nat statistics: inside local translations 0
expected_fault: NAT configuration is missing or not applied

symptom: Only one internal host can access the internet
topology_note: Multiple PCs share one public IP
show_outputs: show ip nat translations: only one inside local address translated
expected_fault: PAT overload is not configured correctly

symptom: NAT translations exist but internet replies never return
topology_note: R1 performs NAT toward ISP
show_outputs: show ip nat translations: translations present; show ip route: missing default route
expected_fault: Router lacks a route toward the ISP

symptom: Wireless clients connect to Wi-Fi but receive no IP address
topology_note: Access point connects to switch VLAN 50
show_outputs: show vlan brief: VLAN 50 missing on switch
expected_fault: Wireless client VLAN is not configured on the switch

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi connects but cannot reach the internet
topology_note: Guest SSID mapped to VLAN 60
show_outputs: show interfaces trunk: VLAN 60 not allowed
expected_fault: Guest VLAN is not carried across the trunk

symptom: Wireless client repeatedly disconnects
topology_note: Access point serves several clients on same channel
show_outputs: show controller/AP status: channel overlap detected
expected_fault: Wireless channel interference is causing instability

symptom: Wireless client connects but cannot reach internal resources
topology_note: Corporate SSID should provide access to internal VLAN 70
show_outputs: show wlan configuration: SSID mapped to guest VLAN 60
expected_fault: Corporate SSID is mapped to the wrong VLAN
